player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly interpreted the question as asking for a comparison between the "talented" and "not talented" groups within the accepted population, which led me to compare 81% and 87%. However, the question asks if the chance of brown eyes decreases *when talent* is present, implying a comparison between the overall probability of brown eyes in accepted students (marginal) versus the probability given talent (conditional). I failed to calculate the overall probability $P(\text{Brown Eyes} | \text{Accepted})$ by weighting the subgroup probabilities by the prevalence of talent and non-talent within the accepted group. Next time, I will first calculate the total probability of brown eyes for accepted students using the law of total probability: $P(B|A) = P(B|A,T)P(T|A) + P(B|A,\neg T)P(\neg T|A)$. I will then compare this marginal value to the conditional value $P(B|A,T) = 81\%$ to determine the correct answer.
